First substantive scan filling the Tier 1 business-bundle pricing envelope. Captured 9 entries in shared/market-scans.jsonl covering Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Raycast, Notion (pricing + AI bundling strategy), Setapp (standard + AI+ tiers), one competitive-observation on credit-allowance adoption, one assumption-check on heavy-user skew, and one observation on the Tier 1 pricing gap.

Key findings:
1. Solo dev-tool price anchors cluster at $8-$20/mo (Raycast $8, Copilot Pro $10, Cursor Pro $20, Notion Plus $10). Next cluster at $39-$60 (Copilot Pro+ $39, Cursor Pro+ $60).
2. The $29-$49/mo Tier 1 target sits in the trough between these clusters — no dominant comp at that price point.
3. Multi-app bundle comps (Setapp) top out at $15 standard, $24 AI+. Vrooli's $29-$49 is materially above this ceiling; can't position as 'bundle of apps' at that price.
4. Notion has converged on 'AI bundled into every paid tier' rather than AI-as-add-on. Directly supports Vrooli's integrated-gateway positioning.
5. Credit-allowance-plus-overage billing is now category-standard (Cursor 3x/20x, Setapp AI+ 10/125/250, Notion Custom Agents $10/1K credits). The Vrooli financial model's assumed billing shape is no longer an experiment.
6. Indirect evidence for the 'heavy users are multi-x mainstream' assumption — competitor tier spreads of 3x-25x usage are consistent with the shape, though not direct user-usage data.

Decisions raised: dec-1777061048708846767 (benchmark-update — populate BENCHMARKS.md); dec-1777061056395576280 (pricing-decision — revisit Tier 1 bracket given two-cluster trough).
